newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner poised to win Aasgard B - source.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner poised to win Aasgard B - source.

text.p: Norwegian shipbuilding and engineering group Kvaerner appeared on Thursday to have won the race for the Aasgard B contract ahead of its main offshore rival Aker Maritime ASA, an industry source said.

The seven billion crown contract is for a semi-submersible gas platform, Aasgard B, for the field which lies off mid-Norway. It is expected to be the largest to be awarded for such a system in the Norwegian and British oil sectors in 1997.
The source said the board of Aasgard operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS was meeting on Thursday to agree its final decision on the contract.

Statoil submitted to the licence partners this week its proposal that Kvaerner should build Aasgard B, the source said. The partners were given a week to assess the proposal, but it would be unusual if the partners failed to back the operator's plan, he said.

"Statoil will make a decision at its board meeting today conditional of the approval of the licence partners," said the source. "Aker is close but for various reasons the contract will go to Kvaerner."
Formally Brown & Root were also in the bidding for the deal but industry sources said early in January that it was out of the race.
